{{Short description|American basketball player (born 2000)}} {{Use American English|date=July 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=July 2024}} {{Infobox basketball biography | name = Craig Porter Jr. | image = Craig Porter Jr. (53368474868) (cropped).jpg | caption = Porter with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in 2023 | position = [[Point guard]] | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 1 | weight_lbs = 180 | league = [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] | team = Cleveland Cavaliers | number = 9 | birth_date = {{birth date and age|2000|2|26}} | birth_place = [[Terre Haute, Indiana]], U.S. | high_school = [[Terre Haute South Vigo High School|South]]
(Terre Haute, Indiana) | college = * [[Vincennes Trailblazers men's basketball|Vincennes]] (2018–2019) * [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]] (2020–2023) | draft_year = 2023 | career_start = 2023 | years1 = {{nbay|2023|start}}–present | team1= [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] | years2 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]]–[[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025]] | team2 = →[[Cleveland Charge]] | highlights = * Third-team All-[[American Athletic Conference|AAC]] (2023) * [[National Junior College Athletic Association|NJCAA]] national champion (2019) }} '''Craig Porter Jr.''' (born February 26, 2000) is an American [[basketball]] player for the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played college basketball for the [[Vincennes Trailblazers men's basketball|Vincennes Trailblazers]] and the [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State Shockers]]. ==Early life and high school career== {{BLP unreferenced section|date=March 2025}} Porter Jr. was born on February 26, 2000, and grew up in [[Terre Haute, Indiana]], where he attended [[Terre Haute South Vigo High School]]. During high school, he was named to the Indiana Basketball Coaches Association's Senior All-State Team and lead his team to the 4A state quarterfinals. ==College career== ===Vincennes=== Porter Jr. started his collegiate career with the [[Vincennes Trailblazers]], where he helped lead them to a combined 62–7 record over two seasons and a [[NJCAA]] national championship in 2019.{{cite web |title=Craig Porter Jr. |url=https://goshockers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/craig-porter-jr-/7213 |website=Whicita State Athletics |access-date=25 June 2023}} After two seasons with the Trailblazers, he committed to [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]].{{cite web |last1=Rocha |first1=Taylor |title=Junior-college point guard Craig Porter commits to Wichita State |url=https://www.ksn.com/sports/shockers/junior-college-point-guard-craig-porter-commits-to-wichita-state/ |website=KSN-TV |access-date=25 June 2023}} ===Wichita State=== ====2020–21 season==== In his first season with the [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Shockers]], Porter Jr. played in 19 games, starting in two of them, where he averaged 2.1 points, 2.1 rebounds, and 1.5 assists in 12.9 minutes per game.{{cite web |title=Craig Porter Jr. |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/portecr01.html |website=Basketball Reference |access-date=March 29, 2025}} After the season he entered the transfer portal{{cite web |last1=Marty |first1=Sean |title=Craig Porter Jr. enters the transfer portal |url=https://thesunflower.com/55283/sports/craig-porter-jr-enters-the-transfer-portal/ |website=The Sunflower |access-date=25 June 2023}} but returned to the Shockers. ====2021–22 season==== In his second year at Wichita State, Porter Jr. played in 25 games, starting in 24, in which he averaged 7.3 points, 4.9 rebounds, and 3.6 assists in 26.9 minutes per game. After the season, he entered his name into the transfer portal.{{cite web |title=Craig Porter Jr. becomes the latest Shocker in the portal |url=https://www.kake.com/story/46351822/craig-porter-jr-becomes-the-latest-shocker-in-the-portal |website=KAKE |access-date=25 June 2023}} However Porter Jr. returned after two former Wichita State baseball players formed a [[name, image and likeness]] (NIL) collective called Armchair Strategies.{{cite web |last1=Marty |first1=Sean |title=Craig Porter Jr. returns to WSU due to new NIL Collective |url=https://thesunflower.com/63163/sports/craig-porter-jr-returns-to-wsu-due-to-new-nil-collective/ |website=The Sunflower |access-date=25 June 2023}} ====2022–23 season==== On February 26, 2023, Porter Jr. posted a triple double, recording 15 points, 10 rebounds, and 10 assists, while also adding three steals in a 83–76 over [[2022-23 Tulane Green Wave men's basketball team|Tulane]].{{cite web |title=Porter's triple-double leads Wichita State past Tulane 83-76 |url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-mens-wichita-state-shockers-jaron-pierre-james-rojas-6e923ae39b6147b6aeb584955937576a |website=AP News |access-date=25 June 2023}} He finished the season playing 31 games, starting in 30, putting up 13.5 points, 6.2 rebounds, and 4.9 assists in 33.6 minutes per game, earning third-team All-AAC honors.{{cite web |last1=Henderson |first1=Matt |title=Wichita State's Porter named to all-AAC third team |url=https://www.kwch.com/2023/03/08/wichita-states-porter-named-all-aac-third-team/ |website=KWCH |access-date=25 June 2023}} After the season, Porter Jr. announced that he would forgo his final year of eligibility to declare for the [[NBA draft]].{{cite web |title=ROUNDUP: Craig Porter declares for NBA draft |url=https://www.tribstar.com/sports/roundup-craig-porter-declares-for-nba-draft/article_97ac5cd4-d3e0-11ed-af46-434eb3c3de6c.html |website=Tribune-Star |access-date=25 June 2023}} ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the [[2023 NBA draft]], Porter Jr. signed a two-way contract with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] on July 7, 2023.{{cite web|first=Taylor|last=Eldrige|title=Wichita State's Craig Porter Jr. agrees to two-way NBA contract with Cleveland Cavaliers|url=https://www.kansas.com/sports/college/wichita-state/article276680631.html|work=The Wichita Eagle|date=June 23, 2023|access-date=June 25, 2023}} On November 19, he recorded 21 points, four assists and four rebounds off the bench in a 121–109 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web |date=November 19, 2023 |title=Darius Garland, Craig Porter Jr. lead Cleveland Cavaliers to win over Denver Nuggets |url=https://www.beaconjournal.com/story/sports/pro/cavs/2023/11/19/cleveland-cavaliers-score-last-night-denver-nuggets-darius-garland-stats-craig-porter-jr-evan-mobley/71645853007/ |access-date=November 26, 2023 |work=Akron Beacon Journal|agency=Associated Press}} On February 14, 2024, Porter Jr. signed a standard contract with the Cavaliers,{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Convert Craig Porter Jr. to Standard NBA Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/cavaliers-convert-craig-porter-jr-to-standard-nba-contract|website=NBA.com|date=February 14, 2024|access-date=February 15, 2024}} being [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] several times to the [[Cleveland Charge]] throughout his rookie and sophomore seasons.{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Cleveland Charge Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Cleveland-Charge/34/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 27, 2024}}{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Cleveland
